criterion: The landing page reads as a warm paper sheet ruled by a faint blueprint grid.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the landing page sits on an off-white, warm ground with a faint ruled grid behind its content. Answer no when the ground is plain white, a flat grey, or a dark surface, or when the ruled grid is absent.

criterion: The console reads quieter than the marketing site, dense but organised for repeated scanning.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the signed-in console drops the marketing page's atmosphere for tight rows, restrained colour, and a stable layout built for scanning. Answer no when the console carries oversized heroes, editorial composition, or decoration borrowed from the landing page.

criterion: The hero pills come to rest as a settled heap after falling into the page.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the coloured pills drop into the hero, collide with each other, then settle into a stable pile that stays readable. Answer no when the pills sit in a fixed arrangement from the first paint, or when the pile keeps jittering after everything has landed.

criterion: A hero pill thrown with the pointer scatters the heap, which settles again inside its container.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when dragging or flicking a pill pushes the others aside, after which the pile comes back to rest with every pill still inside the hero area. Answer no when the pills ignore the pointer, or when a pill escapes past the edge of its container.

criterion: Under a reduced-motion preference the hero pills render in a designed static arrangement.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a browser asking for reduced motion receives a deliberate, legible arrangement of the same pills with the simulation idle. Answer no when the simulation still runs, or when the hero renders empty under that preference.

criterion: Every moving thing in the product leaves quickly, arriving slowly, on one shared character.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when entrances, disclosures, hovers and page changes all share one speed and one feel across the marketing site as well as the console. Answer no when one surface snaps while another eases, or when a single element moves on a character of its own.

criterion: A scroll reveal plays once for its band, holding its arrived state afterwards.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a band fades up as it enters the window, then stays in place when the page scrolls back past it. Answer no when the reveal replays on every pass, or when the band's position tracks the scroll position continuously.

criterion: The pill is the dominant shape from the header through the chips to the buttons.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the header, the category chips, the status chips and the buttons are all fully rounded pill forms. Answer no when those elements carry square or lightly softened corners, or when several different corner treatments appear across one page.

criterion: An unavailable control carries a second signal beyond colour alone.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a control that cannot be used shows its state through wording, an icon, or a change of style as well as its colour. Answer no when only the colour changes, so a reader who cannot see the difference receives the same control as an active one.

criterion: At a phone-width window the catalogue stands one column wide, keeping the price beside the minimum on every card.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the catalogue grid collapses to a single column at a narrow window with both figures still on each card. Answer no when the grid keeps two or more columns, when the card overflows sideways, or when either figure is dropped to make room.

criterion: The header is a floating white pill whose right-hand strip becomes a solid orange demo control once the page scrolls past the hero.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the header sits inset from the top as a rounded white bar, carrying a line of text with an inline link at its right which turns into a filled orange control after the hero leaves the window. Answer no when the header is a full-width bar, or when the right-hand strip keeps one form throughout the scroll.

criterion: On the landing page the wordmark is drawn letterform geometry rather than a font glyph.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the brand name on the landing page is rendered as drawn shapes with soft, swelling strokes that a text selection cannot pick up. Answer no when the wordmark is set in a typeface, so selecting the header copies the brand name as text.

criterion: A text link pointed at falls to about two thirds of its resting strength.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when hovering a text link or the wordmark fades the ink noticeably while leaving its position alone. Answer no when a hovered link changes colour family, gains an underline as its only change, or moves on the page.

criterion: Below the tablet width the quote comparison scrolls sideways with its first column pinned in place.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the comparison stays a readable table at a narrow window, scrolling horizontally while the supplier column stays fixed at the left. Answer no when the table reflows into stacked cards, when the first column scrolls away, or when the comparison is only a chart.

criterion: Proving an entitlement on the storefront recomputes the visible price in place, with the page holding its position.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when signing a challenge changes the listing and its price on the same screen, leaving the scroll position where the visitor left it. Answer no when the page reloads, when the catalogue flashes through an empty state, or when the visitor is sent back to the top.

criterion: The landing page carries four capability panels, each illustrated by a working product mock built from the product's own components.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all four panels sit down the landing page, each paired with a live interface fragment showing real seeded content such as an order card moving through its states or a storefront offering a jacket. Answer no when a panel carries a flat picture, an empty placeholder, or nothing at all.
